claims.text: The three primary artifacts describe one and the same trip, not three different ones: EV-TRIP-00113, EV-GPS-00113 and EV-FARE-00113 each carry trip_id TRP-00113, and the trace's first fix at 18:47:10 matches the trip_record's started_at, so the rider's limb-(a) identification burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the record.

Nothing in the trace needs discounting in the rider's favour or against it: coverage is 100%, there are 217 fixes at the nominal 10-second sampling interval, the gaps array is empty and max_gap_sec is 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a), (b) or (c) fires, the trace is unimpaired for policy purposes, and the driven distance can be read straight off the trace without any gap-handling concession.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the rounded trip_record convenience copy, and the trace records 20.18 km against the optimal route of 19.40 km stored on the trip_record: the measured excess is 0.78 km, or 4.02%.

POL-RD-12 excuses only distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider, and in this case that distance is already inside the 19.40 km matched-itinerary baseline the rider was notified of at 18:42:04; the clause's own closing words are that it 'does not excuse excess beyond the matched itinerary', and the trace still runs 0.78 km beyond that matched baseline.

The diversion is the driver's own route and is corroborated independently of the rider's account: the driver wrote in the chat log at 19:03:15 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route', and the rider's sole message in the log is the query 'why are we at hougang' at 19:02:40 — the rider contributed no route instruction at all.

No traffic advisory carries the diversion: EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING, holds weight 0.0, and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, with no LTA advisory covering the Punggol, Hougang or CTE corridors in the 18:41-19:23 window on 5 August 2026, so POL-RD-03's closure exoneration is unavailable to the driver.

The detour cannot be shifted onto the rider: the chat log contains no rider instruction to divert and no message carries a waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run in the driver's favour, its corroboration test is undecidable on this record, and the driver holds no rider-instruction exoneration.

This is not an upfront-quoted trip, so the route-deviation money has not been closed off: fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, POL-RD-11 does not apply, and POL-RD-02 is the operative remedy clause, which would run against the 19.40 km matched-itinerary figure and not the 15.80 km solo reference figure.

If the excess is made out, the POL-RD-02 quantum is not de minimis on the platform's own numbers: the fare_breakdown's recomputed_fare on the matched 19.40 km and 34 min is SGD 25.67, the difference from the SGD 26.83 charged is 1.16, and the amount payable rounds up to SGD 1.20, which is above the SGD 0.50 floor.

Neither profile can decide this case in either direction: the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 471 completed_trips_90d, so no POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation pattern is established on the only fields that clause names, and under POL-GEN-01 the driver's otherwise clean record is credibility weighting only and may not be used to establish any fact about this trip or to carry an adverse finding against the rider.

I do not stretch the arithmetic: measured on the governing trace the excess is 0.78 km, which does not exceed POL-RD-01's 0.8 km absolute gate, and 4.02%, which does not exceed its 20% gate, so on this trip's own evidence the route deviation as pleaded is not established and the POL-RD-01 finding properly reads 'no deviation'.

claims.text: This is a RYDE_POOL trip, so the only correct baseline for any deviation test is the matched-itinerary optimal that the platform computed and quoted at match time, 19.40 km on EV-TRIP-00113. The rider's arithmetic uses the 15.80 km solo_optimal_distance_km figure, which POL-RD-12 carries on the trip_record expressly 'for reference only' and which may not be used as the denominator of the POL-RD-01 test. A claim that measures excess against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. Both figures are on the face of the record (optimal_distance_km 19.40; solo_optimal_distance_km 15.80), so the rider can see exactly why the 28% figure in the claim text is an artefact of the wrong comparator.

Measured the way POL-RD-01 requires, against the trace figure that governs and not the rounded convenience copy on the trip_record, the excess is 0.78 km. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 20.18 km (EV-GPS-00113) and the matched-itinerary optimal is 19.40 km (EV-TRIP-00113), giving an excess of 0.78 km, or 4.02% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH that the excess exceed 20% of optimal AND that it exceed 0.8 km absolute. This excess fails on both limbs: 4.02% is far below 20%, and 0.78 km is below the 0.8 km floor. No deviation is established, and no MATERIAL deviation is anywhere near established. POL-RD-01 then directs the outcome: NO_ACTION, however the rider characterises the trip.

Even on the rider's own theory that the Hougang leg is the objectionable part, POL-RD-12 excludes it before the threshold is applied: distance attributable to collecting a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary 'is never a deviation'. The record confirms the Hougang stop was precisely that — the driver's track is an unbroken 10-second telemetry trace (point_count 217, coverage_pct 100, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0) whose only dwell is the co-rider boarding stop, and the driver's first and last fixes run 18:47:10 to 19:23:10 with no excursus off the matched corridor. The driver is not exonerated for going somewhere he chose; the stop he made was the itinerary the platform sold.

The route was disclosed to the rider in advance, in writing, by the platform itself. Chat message MSG-00113-001, sent 2026-08-05T18:42:04, states: 'Co-rider matched. Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min.' It was read by the rider 27 seconds later, at 18:42:31, and the trip only started at 18:47:10. The claim that the driver 'went off to Hougang in the middle of my trip for no reason' is contradicted by the platform's own pre-trip notice; the Hougang pickup was announced before the vehicle moved. This is not a rider-instruction exoneration under POL-RD-04 — no waypoint_hint is present — but it is the factual answer to the only allegation of arbitrary conduct in the claim.

The rider's own chat entries corroborate the driver and defeat the claim's premise. At 19:02:40 the rider asks 'why are we at hougang'; the driver answers at 19:03:15 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route'. That answer is consistent with the platform's 18:42:04 match notice, and it is the only party account of the Hougang stop anywhere on the record. The counterparty_statement is to the same effect. There is no artifact in the bundle that contradicts it, and no traffic advisory exists that could have forced the route (EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING; none covers the corridor). The driver's conduct was, on this record, exactly what POL-RD-12 describes and excuses.

The trace itself is unimpaired under POL-RD-07: coverage is 100%, the expected and actual sampling intervals both equal 10 seconds, there are no gaps recorded, and the maximum gap is 0.0 seconds. None of limbs (a), (b) or (c) fires, so the excess is measured from a clean trace and needs no independent corroboration. The GPS_TRACE artifact is also COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so there is no POL-GEN-02 discount to disclose or apply. The rider cannot argue the measurement is unsafe: it is the best-quality evidence in the bundle, and it is the artifact that defeats the claim.

The POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not even reached, and where reached it is clean. The clause is consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation or the evidence is otherwise finely balanced; here there is no deviation at all, let alone a material one, and the evidence is not balanced — one trace, one tolerance, both limbs failed. For completeness, the driver's trailing-90-day figure is deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 471, so no pattern can be established on the fields the clause names, and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting any other profile field for the test. No POL-RD-06(a) uplift, no POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is available to the rider on this record.

There is no alternative monetary route left to the rider. POL-RD-02 is the only clause that converts an established deviation into a refund, and no deviation is established, so the recomputation never runs. The fare-breakdown arithmetic confirms there is nothing else to correct: erp_lines carries no entries at all (total 0.00), the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, the promo_discount of 3.00 has already been subtracted from the charge, and the residual money comparison on EV-FARE-00113 yields a refund before rounding of only 1.16 against a charged_total of 26.83 — which is unreachable in any event because the threshold gate in POL-RD-01 fails. POL-GEN-03 then fixes the meaning of the outcome: the rider filed, the charge stands, the present state is preserved, and the ruling value is NO_ACTION.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties are told the same thing: on this trip's own evidence no route deviation is established, so the fare charged stands.

Which baseline governs. This was a RYDE_POOL booking, so under POL-RD-12 the comparator is the matched-itinerary optimal the platform computed and quoted at match time — 19.40 km, carried on EV-TRIP-00113 as optimal_distance_km. The 15.80 km figure the rider has used is solo_optimal_distance_km, which the same record carries expressly 'for reference only'; it is the unmatched single-rider quote and may not be the denominator of the test. That is why the claim's '28% longer' figure does not survive: 20.2 km against 15.8 km is not the comparison the policy makes. The rider's use of the solo figure fails on that ground alone (POL-RD-12). Both figures are on the face of the record (19.40 and 15.80), so the rider can check this directly.

The threshold test (POL-RD-01). The distance that governs is the trace figure, gps_trace.trace_distance_km 20.18 km on EV-GPS-00113 — not the rounded 20.2 km convenience copy on the trip record. Against the 19.40 km matched baseline the excess is 0.78 km, or 4.02% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires both that the excess exceed 20% of optimal and that it exceed 0.8 km in absolute terms. 4.02% is far below 20%, and 0.78 km does not exceed the 0.8 km floor. Both limbs fail, so no deviation exists and the outcome POL-RD-01 directs is NO_ACTION, however the trip is characterised. No MATERIAL deviation is anywhere near reached, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered; for completeness the driver's trailing-90-day figure is deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 471, so no repeat-deviation pattern could be established on the fields that clause names, and the driver's clean record is otherwise credibility weighting only (POL-GEN-01).

The Hougang leg. The 90-second stop at Hougang Central was the platform-matched co-rider pickup. Under POL-RD-12, distance attributable to collecting a co-rider on a matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation, and it is already inside the 19.40 km quoted baseline. The stop was not concealed: the platform's own message MSG-00113-001, sent 18:42:04 and read by the rider at 18:42:31, stated 'Co-rider matched. Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min', and the trip only started at 18:47:10. The driver's chat reply at 19:03:15 ('pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route') is consistent with that. The rider made no route request of any kind, so no rider-instruction exoneration arises and none is needed: POL-RD-04 is unavailable to the driver, not because of any doubt about conduct but because the clause is simply not in play. The driver's conduct is answered: he drove the matched itinerary and is not at fault, and no adverse finding is made against him.

Money. POL-RD-02 converts an established deviation into a refund and does not run where no deviation is established, so the recomputation is never reached. The fare arithmetic confirms there is nothing else to correct: erp_lines carries no entries (total 0.00), there is no airport surcharge (the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport), the 3.00 pool discount has already been subtracted, and the residual comparison on EV-FARE-00113 (charged_total 26.83; recomputed_fare 25.67; difference before rounding 1.16, payable 1.20) is unreachable because the POL-RD-01 gate fails. No billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) arises from any charge line, so no referral is produced. For the rider's benefit: the 26.83 charged is preserved, and the 6.00 contested amount is not refunded.

Escalation. None of the POL-RD-10 triggers fires. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (all TRP-00113); the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (100% coverage, 217 fixes at a 10-second interval, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0.0), so no corroboration question arises; timestamps agree and do not run backwards; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact; the refund does not approach SGD 150; the parties' evidence is not in contradiction (both advocates read the same 0.78 km excess); and every charge line has a counterpart. Confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor. The absence of any LTA traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING and could carry no fact at weight 0.0) is noted but is not needed: nothing in this ruling turns on a closure.

Outcome. The rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands under POL-GEN-03: the charge on EV-FARE-00113 remains as charged, nothing is refunded and nothing is paid to the driver.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this is a RYDE_POOL trip from Punggol MRT to One Raffles Place on 5 August 2026, and the question is whether the charge of SGD 26.83 should be reduced because the driver went to Hougang.

Which distance figure is the right comparator. Because the booking was pooled, POL-RD-12 fixes the baseline as the MATCHED-ITINERARY optimal of 19.40 km recorded on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00113) — the pooled route the platform computed at match time and announced to the rider in writing at 18:42:04 (chat MSG-00113-001, 'one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min', read at 18:42:31, before the trip started at 18:47:10). The 15.8 km figure in the claim is solo_optimal_distance_km, which the same record carries 'for reference only'; measuring excess against it is the wrong field, and the 28% figure in the claim is an artefact of that comparison.

The deviation test. On the governing trace figure — gps_trace.trace_distance_km 20.18 km (EV-GPS-00113), not the rounded 20.2 km convenience copy on the trip record — the excess over 19.40 km is 0.78 km, or 4.02%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 0.8 km absolute and 20% of optimal. It fails both gates. No deviation is established, so POL-RD-02's fare recomputation (which would otherwise have produced a SGD 1.20 refund off the SGD 26.83 charged) never runs, and the disputed charge stands.

The Hougang stop. The trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07: 217 fixes at the nominal 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s, so none of limbs (a)–(c) fires and the measurement needs no independent corroboration. The Hougang leg is the platform-matched co-rider pickup, and POL-RD-12 excludes co-rider collection distance from the baseline in any event; the driver's on-record statement and the chat exchange ('why are we at hougang' / 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route') are consistent with that and nothing in the bundle contradicts it.

Other clauses. POL-RD-03 (road closure) is both unavailable and unnecessary: EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, and no closure was asserted — a missing artifact nobody relies on does not drag the ruling down. POL-RD-04: no rider instruction to divert appears anywhere in the chat log and no message carries a waypoint_hint, so that exoneration cannot be run and does not excuse the driver; it is simply not needed. POL-RD-06: deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 471 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established on the only fields the clause names, no uplift applies and no conduct referral arises. POL-RD-09: the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries (total 0.00), the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and no charge line lacks a counterpart, so no pass-through or billing-integrity correction or referral arises. POL-RD-11 does not apply: the fare model is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null. Profiles from either side are credibility weighting only under POL-GEN-01 and decide nothing here.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: all three primary artifacts carry trip_id TRP-00113 and consistent timestamps, the trace is clean, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact, and the refund is nil. The confidence cap rests on the two artifacts carrying the deciding facts — EV-TRIP-00113 and EV-GPS-00113 — both at weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0 and the confidence of 0.93 sits well above the 0.70 floor.

Outcome: the rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands — the SGD 26.83 charge remains payable and no refund is due.

ruling.explanation: Both advocates measured this trip the same way and I agree with them, so here is the arithmetic in plain terms. This was a RYDE_POOL booking, and POL-RD-12 makes the matched-itinerary optimal of 19.40 km, quoted when the co-rider was matched, the correct baseline (EV-TRIP-00113). The 15.80 km solo_optimal_distance_km is carried 'for reference only'; the 28% longer figure in the claim is measured against that reference figure and is not the test. The governing distance is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00113): 217 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s, so it is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 and no discount and no independent corroboration is needed. The trace records 20.18 km. Excess = 20.18 - 19.40 = 0.78 km, which is 4.02% of the matched optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be greater than 0.8 km absolute AND greater than 20% of optimal; both gates must pass. 0.78 km and 4.02% fail both. No deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 directs the outcome to NO_ACTION however the trip felt. Note the trap the clause closes: the trip record's rounded actual_distance_km of 20.2 would give exactly 0.8 km and read as material, which is precisely why POL-RD-01 says the trace figure, not the rounded convenience copy, governs. The Hougang leg does not change this: the platform announced the pooled route and the 19.4 km estimate at 18:42:04, read by the rider at 18:42:31, before the trip started at 18:47:10 (EV-CHAT-00113), and POL-RD-12 excludes co-rider collection distance from the test in any event. No rider instruction to divert appears in the chat and no message carries a waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 exonerates nothing either. Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02 never runs and no distance or time refund is available; for transparency only, a recomputation on 19.40 km and 34 min would give 25.67 against the 26.83 charged, a difference of 1.16 (1.20 rounded up), and that route is closed at the threshold. There is no billing-integrity correction to make: erp_lines is empty (0.00), the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither starts nor ends at an airport, and the 3.00 pool discount was already subtracted, so POL-RD-09(4) produces nothing and no referral issues. The driver's record is clean - deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 471 completed trips in 90 days - so POL-RD-06 is not engaged, no pattern is established and no conduct referral follows; profile fields are credibility weighting only under POL-GEN-01. The missing LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-00113-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) is disclosed by the rider's own claim, carries no fact, and is not needed because POL-RD-12, not POL-RD-03, decides this case. The driver's claim that the chat log corroborated the route was discarded at the citation stage for citing that missing artifact without naming its issue code; its substance is covered by the surviving chat evidence. Nothing in the ruling rests on an artifact below weight 1.0, so confidence is not capped below 1.0. The charge of SGD 26.83 stands and the present state is preserved.

ledger.claim: The three primary artifacts describe one and the same trip, not three different ones: EV-TRIP-00113, EV-GPS-00113 and EV-FARE-00113 each carry trip_id TRP-00113, and the trace's first fix at 18:47:10 matches the trip_record's started_at, so the rider's limb-(a) identification burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the record.

Nothing in the trace needs discounting in the rider's favour or against it: coverage is 100%, there are 217 fixes at the nominal 10-second sampling interval, the gaps array is empty and max_gap_sec is 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a), (b) or (c) fires, the trace is unimpaired for policy purposes, and the driven distance can be read straight off the trace without any gap-handling concession.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the rounded trip_record convenience copy, and the trace records 20.18 km against the optimal route of 19.40 km stored on the trip_record: the measured excess is 0.78 km, or 4.02%.

POL-RD-12 excuses only distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider, and in this case that distance is already inside the 19.40 km matched-itinerary baseline the rider was notified of at 18:42:04; the clause's own closing words are that it 'does not excuse excess beyond the matched itinerary', and the trace still runs 0.78 km beyond that matched baseline.

The diversion is the driver's own route and is corroborated independently of the rider's account: the driver wrote in the chat log at 19:03:15 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route', and the rider's sole message in the log is the query 'why are we at hougang' at 19:02:40 — the rider contributed no route instruction at all.

No traffic advisory carries the diversion: EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING, holds weight 0.0, and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, with no LTA advisory covering the Punggol, Hougang or CTE corridors in the 18:41-19:23 window on 5 August 2026, so POL-RD-03's closure exoneration is unavailable to the driver.

The detour cannot be shifted onto the rider: the chat log contains no rider instruction to divert and no message carries a waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run in the driver's favour, its corroboration test is undecidable on this record, and the driver holds no rider-instruction exoneration.

This is not an upfront-quoted trip, so the route-deviation money has not been closed off: fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, POL-RD-11 does not apply, and POL-RD-02 is the operative remedy clause, which would run against the 19.40 km matched-itinerary figure and not the 15.80 km solo reference figure.

If the excess is made out, the POL-RD-02 quantum is not de minimis on the platform's own numbers: the fare_breakdown's recomputed_fare on the matched 19.40 km and 34 min is SGD 25.67, the difference from the SGD 26.83 charged is 1.16, and the amount payable rounds up to SGD 1.20, which is above the SGD 0.50 floor.

Neither profile can decide this case in either direction: the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 471 completed_trips_90d, so no POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation pattern is established on the only fields that clause names, and under POL-GEN-01 the driver's otherwise clean record is credibility weighting only and may not be used to establish any fact about this trip or to carry an adverse finding against the rider.

I do not stretch the arithmetic: measured on the governing trace the excess is 0.78 km, which does not exceed POL-RD-01's 0.8 km absolute gate, and 4.02%, which does not exceed its 20% gate, so on this trip's own evidence the route deviation as pleaded is not established and the POL-RD-01 finding properly reads 'no deviation'.

This is a RYDE_POOL trip, so the only correct baseline for any deviation test is the matched-itinerary optimal that the platform computed and quoted at match time, 19.40 km on EV-TRIP-00113. The rider's arithmetic uses the 15.80 km solo_optimal_distance_km figure, which POL-RD-12 carries on the trip_record expressly 'for reference only' and which may not be used as the denominator of the POL-RD-01 test. A claim that measures excess against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. Both figures are on the face of the record (optimal_distance_km 19.40; solo_optimal_distance_km 15.80), so the rider can see exactly why the 28% figure in the claim text is an artefact of the wrong comparator.

Measured the way POL-RD-01 requires, against the trace figure that governs and not the rounded convenience copy on the trip_record, the excess is 0.78 km. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 20.18 km (EV-GPS-00113) and the matched-itinerary optimal is 19.40 km (EV-TRIP-00113), giving an excess of 0.78 km, or 4.02% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH that the excess exceed 20% of optimal AND that it exceed 0.8 km absolute. This excess fails on both limbs: 4.02% is far below 20%, and 0.78 km is below the 0.8 km floor. No deviation is established, and no MATERIAL deviation is anywhere near established. POL-RD-01 then directs the outcome: NO_ACTION, however the rider characterises the trip.

Even on the rider's own theory that the Hougang leg is the objectionable part, POL-RD-12 excludes it before the threshold is applied: distance attributable to collecting a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary 'is never a deviation'. The record confirms the Hougang stop was precisely that — the driver's track is an unbroken 10-second telemetry trace (point_count 217, coverage_pct 100, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0) whose only dwell is the co-rider boarding stop, and the driver's first and last fixes run 18:47:10 to 19:23:10 with no excursus off the matched corridor. The driver is not exonerated for going somewhere he chose; the stop he made was the itinerary the platform sold.

The route was disclosed to the rider in advance, in writing, by the platform itself. Chat message MSG-00113-001, sent 2026-08-05T18:42:04, states: 'Co-rider matched. Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min.' It was read by the rider 27 seconds later, at 18:42:31, and the trip only started at 18:47:10. The claim that the driver 'went off to Hougang in the middle of my trip for no reason' is contradicted by the platform's own pre-trip notice; the Hougang pickup was announced before the vehicle moved. This is not a rider-instruction exoneration under POL-RD-04 — no waypoint_hint is present — but it is the factual answer to the only allegation of arbitrary conduct in the claim.

At 19:02:40 the rider asks 'why are we at hougang'; the driver answers at 19:03:15 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route'. That answer is consistent with the platform's 18:42:04 match notice, and it is the only party account of the Hougang stop anywhere on the record. The counterparty_statement is to the same effect. There is no artifact in the bundle that contradicts it, and no traffic advisory exists that could have forced the route (EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING; none covers the corridor).
